options.metric: Annual total number of people killed as motorists and annual total number of people killed as cyclists, calculated as the sums of number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed.
options.denominator: None; annual totals of recorded people killed.
options.grouping: Calendar year, with two road-user series: motorist and cyclist.
options.reason: Annual counts are the most direct way to compare the recorded number of motorist and cyclist deaths year by year.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year from 2013 to 2025: 72–139 motorist deaths per year versus 10–31 cyclist deaths.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the question by summing the motorist-killed and cyclist-killed fields across all police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash records dated January 1, 2013 through December 31, 2025, separately for each calendar year, with no denominator. Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths every year, ranging from 72 in 2016 to 139 in 2020, while cyclist deaths ranged from 10 in 2018 to 31 in both 2019 and 2023. Annual counts are a defensible comparison of recorded fatality burden, but they do not measure per-trip or per-person risk or adjust for exposure. The check found 2,132,218 in-scope rows, observed dates spanning January 1 through December 31 in every year (without ruling out within-year reporting gaps), and zero missing values in either death field; row counts ranged from 203,742 in 2013 to 85,546 in 2025, and all 381 records dated 2013-01-01 were kept in 2013 despite the possible date-default pileup, so their actual crash year is unverified.

options.metric: For each year, cyclist deaths divided by the sum of cyclist and motorist deaths, and motorist deaths divided by that same sum; expressed as percentages.
options.denominator: Annual total of cyclist plus motorist deaths.
options.grouping: Calendar year, with shares split between motorist and cyclist deaths.
options.reason: Annual shares compare the relative composition of motorist and cyclist deaths even when their combined total varies by year.
options.answer: Motorists accounted for 72.6%–90.9% and cyclists for 9.1%–27.4% of combined motorist-plus-cyclist deaths, with the cyclist share highest in 2019 and lowest in 2013.
options.interpretation: This framing answers the question as a yearly composition measure: for each calendar year from 2013 through 2025, cyclist deaths are divided by the sum of cyclist and motorist deaths and motorist deaths are divided by that same sum, using police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash records dated within those years. Motorists made up 72.6%–90.9% of this combined total and cyclists 9.1%–27.4%; the cyclist share was highest in 2019 and lowest in 2013. Shares are defensible for comparing relative composition, but the denominator excludes deaths of other road-user types and says nothing about absolute fatality totals or exposure-adjusted risk. The check found 2,132,218 in-scope rows, observed dates spanning January 1 through December 31 in every year (without ruling out within-year reporting gaps), and zero missing values in either death field; 381 records dated 2013-01-01 were retained in 2013 despite the possible date-default pileup, leaving their actual crash year unverified.
